title: Cancer Survivorship: Gaps and Needs in Medical Education
summary:
Background

In Germany, several million people have survived cancer for at least five years. Many of them continue to experience physical or psychological effects long after completing their initial treatment. As a result, they often require long-term, individually tailored medical follow-up that goes beyond the usual aftercare provided during the first years.

So far, however, only a small proportion of those affected receive structured and specialized long-term care. For the majority, comprehensive services are not yet widely available. At the same time, it can be expected that in the future more survivors will seek such care and more physicians will be involved in providing it. This makes targeted and well-structured medical training increasingly important.

Research Questions

The project examines how well physicians in Germany are currently prepared to provide long-term care for people who have survived cancer.

In particular, it addresses the following questions:

How do physicians assess their own knowledge and skills in this area?

Where do they perceive uncertainties or gaps in knowledge?

Which topics should receive greater emphasis in medical training?

How can collaboration between different medical specialties be improved?

The aim is to identify existing gaps and develop concrete approaches to improve professional qualification.

Methods

The project consists of three consecutive components:

Online survey:
Physicians from different specialties complete a questionnaire. Among other aspects, they report how confident they feel in caring for this patient group and what training needs they perceive.

In-depth group discussions:
In moderated online discussions, physicians describe their practical experiences in more detail, including challenges they face and shortcomings in current training opportunities.

Multi-stage consensus process:
In several survey rounds, common priorities and key topics are identified and refined, allowing experts from different specialties to reach agreement.

Participants are recruited through professional medical associations and existing networks.

Project Goal

The results will serve as a basis for developing future training programs that are closely aligned with actual needs. In the long term, the project aims to improve the quality and coordination of care for all people who have survived cancer.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Physicians from medical specialties involved in the care of survivors according to clinical guidelines, as well as survivorship experts and decision-makers
-Clinical practice in Germany (outpatient or inpatient setting)
-Sufficient proficiency in the German language
Exclusion criteria:
- Insufficient proficiency in the German language
